born: 农业在中原积累了上千年,到公元前二千纪前期,洛阳盆地出现了辐射广大区域的王权和最早的宫城。主流看法是它对应文献中的夏,但二里头没有出土文字,这个对应仍在争论中。

After centuries of farming built up wealth on the Central Plains, a royal power with the earliest known palace city emerged in the Luoyang basin in the early second millennium BCE. Mainstream scholars link it to the Xia of later texts, but no writing has been found at Erlitou, so the match remains debated.
rule: 统治靠垄断「礼」:宫城里的宫殿用于仪式,青铜爵和绿松石礼器只能由王权作坊铸造、按身份分配。谁能主持祭祀、谁能用什么器物,就是权力的等级表。

Rule rested on a monopoly of ritual: palace ceremonies, and bronze and turquoise regalia that only royal workshops could make and only ranked elites could hold. Who presided over the rites, and who used which vessels, was the visible ladder of power.
money: 经济的根基是粟和稻的农业;都邑同时控制着铜、锡、绿松石等远方原料的输入,把稀缺资源变成礼器,再把礼器变成权威。

The economy rested on millet and rice farming. The capital also controlled long-distance flows of copper, tin, and turquoise, turning scarce materials into ritual objects — and ritual objects into authority.
power: 变强靠技术与礼制的辐射:二里头掌握了当时最复杂的青铜合金铸造,它的礼器样式和宫室布局被周边聚落模仿——影响力走得比疆界更远。

Its strength radiated through technology and ritual. Erlitou mastered the most complex bronze casting of its day, and neighboring communities copied its vessel styles and palace layouts — its influence traveled farther than any border.
fall: 公元前1600年前后,二里头都邑衰落,郑州一带的二里岗文化(早商)兴起并取而代之。文献说商汤灭夏,考古只能看到权力中心的转移;两者如何对应,尚无定论。

Around 1600 BCE the Erlitou capital declined, and the Erligang culture (early Shang) around Zhengzhou rose in its place. Texts say Tang of Shang overthrew the Xia; archaeology shows only a shift of the power center, and how the two accounts fit together remains unsettled.
legacy: 宫城居中、中轴对称的都城格局,和用青铜礼器标记等级的传统,被商周继承并放大——后世中国王朝的许多基本语法在这里初见雏形,所以考古学家称它为「最早的中国」。

Its centered, axial palace-city plan and its use of bronze ritual vessels to mark rank were inherited and amplified by the Shang and Zhou. Many basic grammars of later Chinese dynasties first appear here — which is why archaeologists call it 'the earliest China'.

born: 主流看法是商人取代了二里头代表的旧王权,文献称之为商汤灭夏。新王权把占卜和祭祀抓在自己手里,让神权与王权合为一体,统治从此有了宗教引擎。

The mainstream view is that the Shang displaced the older royal power represented by Erlitou — texts call it Tang's conquest of the Xia. The new kings took divination and sacrifice into their own hands, fusing religious and royal authority into a single engine of rule.
rule: 商王既是君主也是最高祭司:大事必占卜,由王沟通祖先与上帝,刻在甲骨上的问答就是国家档案。王直接控制王畿,外围方国靠联盟、联姻与征伐维系,服从并不稳固。

The Shang king was both monarch and chief priest: major decisions went through divination, with the king mediating between the ancestors and the high god, and the questions carved on oracle bones became state archives. He ruled the royal domain directly, while outer polities were held by alliance, marriage, and war — and their obedience was never secure.
money: 经济以农业为本,青铜铸造是王室垄断的顶级产业;海贝作为珍贵财物流通,常被王赏赐给臣下。铸一件大鼎要动员数百工匠,本身就是国力的展示。

Farming was the economic base, and bronze casting was the top industry, monopolized by the court. Cowrie shells circulated as precious wealth, often granted by the king as rewards. Casting a great cauldron took hundreds of craftsmen — itself a display of state power.
power: 变强靠青铜兵器和马拉战车组成的军队,商王频繁亲征周边方国;武丁时代最盛,王后妇好也统兵出征,甲骨文里记着她的战功。

Strength came from armies with bronze weapons and horse-drawn chariots, and Shang kings campaigned constantly against neighboring polities. The peak came under Wu Ding, whose consort Fu Hao herself led troops — her victories are recorded on the oracle bones.
fall: 主流看法是多因叠加:晚期王室连年对东夷用兵消耗国力,内部也有紧张;周人在西方坐大,牧野一战商军崩溃。纣王荒暴的形象主要出自周人的记载,当有夸张成分。

The mainstream view points to converging causes: late Shang kings drained the state in long wars against the eastern peoples while tensions grew at court, and the Zhou rose in the west until the Shang army collapsed at Muye. The image of the last king as a monster comes mainly from Zhou records, and is likely exaggerated.
legacy: 甲骨文是汉字的直系祖先,三千多年前的问卜今天仍能被读出;青铜礼器与祖先崇拜奠定了中华礼制的底色。中国有文字可考的历史,从商开始。

Oracle-bone script is the direct ancestor of Chinese characters — questions asked three thousand years ago can still be read today. Bronze ritual vessels and ancestor worship set the tone of Chinese ritual culture, and China's documented history begins with the Shang.

born: 牧野之战后,人口不多的周人面对辽阔的商朝故地,发明了一套治理方案:大封宗亲功臣到各地建国,像撒网一样铺开据点。又提出「天命」——上天把统治权交给有德者,商失德所以周代之,征服由此获得道义解释。

After Muye, the small Zhou people faced the vast former Shang lands and invented a solution: granting kinsmen and allies fiefs across the realm, spreading strongholds like a net. They also proclaimed the Mandate of Heaven — rule belongs to the virtuous, and the Shang had forfeited it — giving conquest a moral explanation.
rule: 统治靠宗法加封建:天子、诸侯、卿大夫按血缘层层分封,嫡长子继承定下名分;周公制礼作乐,用礼仪和音乐把等级刻进日常生活。整套秩序靠亲情与仪式维系,而不靠常备官僚。

Rule combined kinship law with enfeoffment: king, lords, and ministers were ranked by blood, with succession fixed on the eldest son of the principal wife. The Duke of Zhou codified rites and music that carved hierarchy into daily life. The whole order ran on kinship and ceremony, not on a standing bureaucracy.
money: 经济以农业为本,据后世记载,土地按「井田」划分,由庶民耕种、贵族收取劳役地租——井田的实际形态学界仍有争论。青铜器既是礼器也是财富,王的赏赐就是政治货币。

The economy rested on farming. Later texts describe land divided into 'well-field' grids worked by commoners for aristocratic lords, though how literally this operated is still debated. Bronzes were both ritual objects and wealth — royal gifts of bronze were political currency.
power: 变强靠封建网络的扩张:每个封国都是一座前哨,把周人的语言、礼制和农业带到边地;成康之治时鼎盛,后世追述称那时刑罚长期搁置不用。

Strength grew through the expanding web of fiefs: each was an outpost carrying Zhou language, ritual, and agriculture to the frontiers. The peak came under kings Cheng and Kang, when — later chroniclers claimed — punishments went unused for decades.
fall: 主流看法是多因叠加:几代之后血缘变远,诸侯离心,王室直辖的土地与军队不断缩水;厉王与民争利引发国人暴动,幽王废嫡引来申侯联合犬戎攻破镐京(前771年)。平王东迁洛邑,王权从此名存实亡。

The mainstream view sees converging causes: as generations passed, kinship ties thinned and the lords drifted away, while the royal domain and army kept shrinking. King Li's grab at profits sparked a popular uprising; King You's tampering with the succession provoked an attack that sacked the capital in 771 BCE. The court fled east to Luoyi, and real royal power was gone.
legacy: 「天命靡常,惟德是辅」把政权合法性和统治者的德行绑在一起,成为此后三千年中国政治哲学的底层逻辑;宗法观念渗入中国的家庭伦理;青铜器何尊铭文「宅兹中国」,是「中国」一词最早的实物见证。

The idea that Heaven's mandate follows virtue tied legitimacy to a ruler's conduct — the base code of Chinese political philosophy for three millennia. Zhou kinship norms seeped into Chinese family ethics, and the He zun bronze's inscription 'dwelling in Zhongguo' is the earliest physical witness of the term 'Middle Kingdom'.

born: 周平王东迁后,王室失去了关中的土地和军队,只剩天下共主的名分;权力出现真空,秩序只能由最强的诸侯来维持——霸主时代由此开场。

After the Zhou court fled east it lost its lands and armies in the Wei valley, keeping only the title of overlord. Into the power vacuum stepped the strongest lords, who alone could keep order — the age of hegemons had begun.
rule: 这个时代没有统一政权:周天子是名义共主,实际秩序靠霸主召集会盟来维持,齐桓公、晋文公都打「尊王攘夷」的旗号——尊天子是外衣,当盟主是实质。列国内部,权力又渐渐从国君滑向卿大夫家族。

No single power ruled this era. The Zhou king was overlord in name only; real order came from hegemons summoning the lords to sworn covenants under the banner of 'honor the king, repel the tribes' — reverence was the costume, leadership the substance. Within each state, power meanwhile slid from rulers to ministerial clans.
money: 经济在战争间隙里升级:铁器开始出现,牛耕初步推广,荒地被开垦成私田;各国自铸铜币,商人往来列国之间,郑国等地的市场已相当活跃。

The economy upgraded between wars: iron tools appeared, ox-drawn plowing began to spread, and wasteland became private fields. States minted their own bronze coins, and merchants moved across borders — markets in states like Zheng were already lively.
power: 变强的逻辑是兼并:一百多个诸侯国互相吞并到只剩十几个,小国靠会盟求生,大国靠灭国扩张;军队规模随之膨胀,战争从贵族车战滑向全民动员的前夜。

The logic of strength was annexation: over a hundred states devoured one another down to a dozen or so, small ones surviving by covenant, great ones growing by conquest. Armies swelled accordingly, and war drifted from aristocratic chariot duels toward the eve of mass mobilization.
fall: 这个格局的终结来自内部:各国的卿大夫家族坐大,反过来架空国君;前453年晋国的赵、魏、韩三家瓜分晋国,连「君臣名分」这最后一层旧秩序也破了——历史进入更赤裸的战国。

The order ended from within: ministerial clans grew strong enough to hollow out their own rulers. In 453 BCE three such clans carved up the great state of Jin, breaking even the last pretense of lord-and-vassal order — history entered the more naked age of the Warring States.
legacy: 旧秩序松动的缝隙里长出了中国思想的源头:孔子办不问出身的私学,老子留下《道德经》,《诗经》《左传》在此定型。此后中国人讨论政治与道德的基本词汇,大半在这三百年里铸成。

In the cracks of the loosening old order grew the wellspring of Chinese thought: Confucius opened schools that ignored birth, Laozi left the Daodejing, and classics like the Book of Songs took shape. Much of the basic vocabulary Chinese still use to discuss politics and morality was forged in these three centuries.

born: 三家分晋撕掉了旧秩序的最后遮羞布,七个大国进入你死我活的淘汰赛;生存压力逼着各国变法——谁不改革,谁就出局。

The partition of Jin tore away the old order's last fig leaf, and seven great powers entered a life-or-death elimination round. Survival pressure forced reform on everyone — change, or be knocked out.
rule: 这个时代没有统一政权,统治的新形态却在竞争中诞生:各国君主绕开世袭贵族,把农民直接编入国家户籍,派拿薪水的官僚去管理郡县。变法最彻底的秦,把这台机器造得最完整。

No unified power existed, but a new form of rule was born in the contest: rulers bypassed hereditary nobles, registered peasants directly with the state, and sent salaried officials to run counties. Qin, the most thorough reformer, built this machine most completely.
money: 铁犁与牛耕让荒地变良田,李冰修的都江堰至今仍在灌溉成都平原;各国铸造形状各异的货币,临淄这样的都会人口数十万。各国的财政,已能支撑数十万人规模的大军。

Iron plows and ox power turned wasteland into farmland, and Li Bing's Dujiangyan waterworks still irrigate the Chengdu plain today. States minted coins of wildly different shapes, and cities like Linzi held hundreds of thousands of people. State finances could now sustain armies numbering in the hundreds of thousands.
power: 变强靠制度:魏国李悝、楚国吴起、秦国商鞅先后变法,军功爵让平民靠战功换地位,郡县制让君主的命令直达基层。战争随之升级为倾国动员的总体战,长平之战赵国损失的军队,据《史记》记载达四十余万——数字或有夸大。

Strength came from institutions: reformers like Li Kui, Wu Qi, and Shang Yang rebuilt their states, merit ranks let commoners rise through battlefield service, and county administration carried the ruler's orders down to the village. War escalated into total mobilization — at Changping, Zhao's losses were recorded (perhaps with exaggeration) at over four hundred thousand.
fall: 格局的终结者是秦:据有关中和巴蜀两大粮仓,变法最彻底、动员最高效,再配上远交近攻的外交;从前230年起十年之内,六国次第而亡,前221年天下归一。

Qin ended the era: holding the twin granaries of the Wei valley and Sichuan, running the most thorough reforms and the most efficient mobilization, and pairing them with divide-and-conquer diplomacy. From 230 BCE it destroyed the six rival states within a decade, uniting the realm in 221 BCE.
legacy: 稷下学宫里儒道法墨吵出的百家争鸣,是中国思想史最富创造力的时期;官僚制、郡县制、户籍制这些国家机器零件的原型也在此锻成。此后两千年,中国人治国的工具箱大半来自战国。

The Hundred Schools debating at the Jixia academy made this the most creative period in Chinese intellectual history. The prototypes of bureaucracy, county administration, and household registration — core parts of the state machine — were also forged here. For the next two millennia, much of China's governing toolkit came from the Warring States.
